results.title: Weekly Pricing Pulse — September 7, 2026 | AIForge Works
highlights:
The Weekly Pricing Pulse tracks what changed in published GPU cloud pricing across AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI, CoreWeave, Lambda, Vultr, Nebius, and Crusoe over the last week. AIForge Works compares each new harvest with the prior verified harvest and highlights buyer-relevant movement: comparable on-demand price changes, New Silicon, restored / expanded visibility, newly absent exact provider + region + instance/SKU observations, and likely price/SKU rolls.

...

## Editor's note

Comparable public on-demand per-GPU rates were effectively flat again this week. The transaction benchmark was not.

Across the nine providers we track, no directly comparable public on-demand per-GPU rate moved more than our 1% reporting threshold. The Ornn × ICE transaction-price index (OCPI) rose across all four tracked families over the seven days through September 8: H200 increased 8.9% to $4.91 per GPU-hour, H100 SXM increased 8.8% to $3.08, B200 increased 5.0% to $6.72, and A100 SXM4 increased 2.0% to $1.02. These OCPI readings are one day newer than the September 7 catalog snapshot and are separate from the catalog-movement result.

For H200, the index now sits above the lowest eligible public offer in our reviewed set, at $4.91 versus Crusoe's $4.29 in Europe (Iceland). B200 is roughly level, at $6.72 versus Lambda's $6.69 listing. Lambda does not publish a complete region for that offer, so these lower catalog rates are leads to verify, not executable quotes.

Catalog changes were visibility changes, not comparable week-over-week repricing above 1%. Twelve observations became newly visible, five returned across Lambda and Vultr, and six exact observations across those same providers were no longer visible. AWS accounted for ten of the newly visible observations: five operating-system variants each of the eight-GPU `p6-b200.48xlarge` in Hyderabad, from $20.08 per GPU-hour, and `p6-b300.48xlarge` in Jakarta, from $28.87. Azure supplied the other two: one- and two-GPU NCads H100 v5 configurations in UK West, both normalized to $9.14 per GPU-hour. The same NCads H100 configurations remained listed in East US at $6.98 per GPU-hour in the same snapshot. UK West was therefore $2.16, or 30.9%, higher per GPU-hour. This is a same-snapshot regional price difference, not a weekly price move.

These catalog observations do not prove a launch, added capacity, retirement, orderability, or current availability. Verify the exact GPU, region, purchase terms, and availability before treating any listing as a buying option.

OCPI, the Ornn Compute Price Index, is a transaction-based benchmark that is separate from the public on-demand catalog prices tracked elsewhere in this Pulse. results.title: 英伟达 H100、B200 租金月涨超 10% | AI头条
highlights:
AI头条 2026-09-07 1176 

# 英伟达多款 GPU 的算力租赁价格正在回升，其中 H100、B200 近一个月涨幅均超过 10%，RTX 5090 涨幅接近 30%。

算力市场数据提供商 Ornn 公布的最新数据显示，截至 2026 年 9 月 5 日，英伟达 B200 租赁价格为每块 GPU 每小时 6.42 美元，近 7 天上涨 6.0%，近 30 天上涨 11.7%。

H100 SXM 租赁价格升至每小时 3.06 美元，近 7 天上涨 6.8%，近 30 天上涨 12.7%。

A100 SXM4 报每小时 1.09 美元，近 7 天和近 30 天分别上涨 5.5% 和 4.4%。

消费级旗舰显卡 RTX 5090 的租赁价格涨幅最高，目前为每小时 0.63 美元，近 7 天上涨 18.0%，近 30 天上涨 27.6%。

H200 的走势有所不同。其最新租赁价格为每小时 4.55 美元，近 7 天上涨 2.6%，但近 30 天仍下跌 7.5%。

Ornn Compute Price Index（OCPI）依据新型云服务商市场的实际成交数据编制，采用成交量加权并进行极值处理，每个交易日结算一次。该指数反映的是 GPU 按需租赁市场价格，不包括预留算力、长期租赁合同和远期合约，也不代表英伟达调整 GPU 硬件售价。

从具体走势看，H100 和 B200 等数据中心 GPU 的租金重新走高，反映训练、推理等 AI 工作负载对高端算力的需求仍在吸收新增供给。

不过，不同型号之间已经出现分化，H100、B200 和 RTX 5090 月内上涨，H200 则尚未收复此前跌幅。

results.title: Neocloud Debt and the GPU Collateral Value Problem | Aethir
highlights:
1. Neocloud debt became a buyer-side question: CoreWeave, the largest listed neocloud, reported roughly $35 billion of debt on its balance sheet at the end of the second quarter of 2026. Debt of that size is no longer just an investor story, because the contracts written to service it are the contracts enterprise compute buyers are asked to sign.
2. GPU-backed debt rests on a depreciation assumption: More than $20 billion of loans across the sector are collateralized by NVIDIA accelerators. Every one of those structures assumes the hardware holds enough value over five to six years to secure the borrowed money against it.
3. GPU collateral value is about to get a public price: Rental rates for H100-class capacity fell from roughly $7 to $10 per hour in early 2024 to $2 to $4 by late 2025. Exchange-traded GPU compute futures now in development would, for the first time, publish a forward curve on that same question.
4. GPU cloud counterparty risk sits inside long contracts: Loan maturities in the sector run roughly five years while the customer contracts pledged against them average closer to three. A buyer signing a multi-year reservation is extending credit to the operator, effectively buying capacity from it.
5. A decentralized GPU cloud has no single balance sheet: Aethir aggregates enterprise GPU capacity from independent operators across 94 countries into one orchestrated pool. With Aethir ACCELERATE, we are adding 10 proprietary mid-sized data centers to our AI compute roster for even more versatile enterprise compute services.

...

A depreciation schedule is an estimate. The rental rate is the mark. H100 class capacity that rented for roughly $7 to $10 dollars per hour in early 2024 was clearing at $2 to $4 dollars by late 2025, and guidance on whether enterprises should rent or own AI compute now treats that decline as the central variable. GPU collateral value moves with the rate card, not with the useful life a finance team selected, which is the same force behind recent GPU cloud pricing moves.

Intercontinental Exchange announced plans with Ornn to launch GPU compute futures contracts referencing a compute price index built on live spot pricing across H100, H200, B200 and RTX 5090 capacity. The contracts are cash settled in US dollars and subject to regulatory approval.

Other exchanges have announced compute futures plans for 2026 as well. When several venues publish a forward price for the same hardware, the argument about GPU collateral value stops being an internal accounting matter.

A ... It gives buyers the same reference for judging whether a multi-year rate quoted today is competitive in year three.

results.title: 컴퓨트 선물 2종, 10월 5일 출시 추진 - TokenPost
highlights:
# 컴퓨트 선물 2종, 10월 5일 출시 추진

 서지우 기자 2026.09.07 07:42 

CME그룹과 실리콘데이터가 엔비디아 H100·B200 GPU 임대료 지수를 추종하는 컴퓨트 선물 2종 출시를 추진한다. 거래 개시는 규제 심사 완료를 전제로 한다.

 

금속 작업대 위에 놓인 그래픽카드와 공구 / TokenPost.ai

컴퓨트 선물 2종이 인공지능(AI) 연산 자원의 임대료 변동을 헤지하는 새 파생상품으로 제도권 시장 진입을 준비하고 있다. 대상은 엔비디아($NVDA) H100과 B200 그래픽처리장치(GPU)의 시간당 임대가격 지수다.

CME그룹(CME Group)과 실리콘데이터(Silicon Data)는 8월 11일 발표에서 규제 심사를 전제로 10월 5일 ‘Silicon Data H100 Rental Index Futures’와 ‘Silicon Data B200 Rental Index Futures’를 출시할 계획이라고 밝혔다. 두 상품은 CME 글로벡스에서 거래되고 CME 클리어포트를 통해 청산 제출이 가능하도록 설계됐다.

컴퓨트 선물은 GPU 자체를 사고파는 계약이 아니다. AI 모델 학습과 추론에 필요한 연산 자원의 임대료를 지수화하고, 이를 기준으로 정산하는 선물 계약이다.

CFTC 산업등록 페이지에 따르면 9월 7일 기준 두 상품은 모두 ‘Approval Pending (45)’ 상태다. 이는 거래 개시가 확정됐다는 뜻이 아니며, 실제 상장은 규제 심사 완료를 전제로 한다.

본지도 앞서 컴퓨트 선물 상장 추진이 규제 심사를 전제로 한다고 전했다. 당시 쟁점은 GPU를 직접 인도받는 구조가 아니라, GPU 임대료와 컴퓨팅 접근성을 표준화된 선물 상품으로 다룰 수 있느냐였다.

상품 구조는 AI 인프라 비용 관리 수요와 맞물려 있다. AI 개발사는 향후 GPU 임대료 상승 위험을 줄이는 수단으로 활용할 수 있고, 데이터센터 사업자는 임대가격 하락 위험을 관리하는 데 쓸 수 있다.

...

연합인포맥스는 7일 시사금융용어 기사에서 컴퓨트 선물을 GPU의 시간당 임대가격 지수를 기초로 한 파생상품이라고 설명했다. AI 학습과 추론 수요가 늘면서 GPU 임대료 변동 위험을 관리할 수단으로 등장했다는 설명이다.

시장 구조상 컴퓨트는 원유나 전력처럼 일정한 가격 기준을 만들기 어려운 자원이다. 같은 GPU라도 공급업체, 지역, 계약 기간, 서비스 수준에 따라 실제 임대가격이 달라질 수 있기 때문이다.

이 때문에 표준화된 지수가 개별 계약의 비용 변동을 얼마나 따라갈지는 상장 이후 거래와 정산 사례를 통해 확인될 문제다. 지수와 실제 계약 조건이 어긋나면 헤지 효과가 제한될 수 있다.

...

CME그룹 공지 기준 두 계약은 뉴욕상업거래소(NYMEX) 규칙을 적용받는다. 고객 테스트는 8월 30일부터 가능하도록 준비됐고, 정식 거래 개시는 10월 5일 규제 심사 완료 여부에 달려 있다.

results.title: AWS GPU Price Increases 2026: What to Do About It
highlights:
AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices for ML in January and again on 1 July 2026, so re-run your GPU budget now. Measure utilization per block, split training from inference, price the portable training half at specialist clouds, and renew only blocks you keep above roughly 70% busy. Production inference inside AWS usually stays put.

...

## The rates as of October 2026

These are the per-accelerator-hour Capacity Block rates on AWS's pricing page at the end of October 2026. Every instance has 8 accelerators, so multiply by 8 for the instance-hour.

| Instance | Accelerator | Region shown | Per accelerator-hour | Per instance-hour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | 8 x B300 | US East (N. Virginia) | $16.146 | $129.17 |
| P6-B200 | 8 x B200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $14.208 | $113.66 |
| P5en | 8 x H200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $7.895 | $63.16 |
| P5e | 8 x H200 | US East (Ohio) | $6.866 | $54.93 |
| P5 | 8 x H100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $5.970 | $47.76 |
| P4de | 8 x A100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $2.546 | $20.37 |

When we first wrote this in September, P6-B300 was about $14.04 and P6-B200 about $12.355, so the published rates have moved up roughly another 15% since. That last point is the one to act on: if you know you need a block in Q1, buying it before January locks today's rate.

highlights:
Bitget Launches GPU Compute Perpetuals

Bitget Launches Industry First H100 and B200 GPU Compute Perpetuals

Victoria, Seychelles, September 8, 2026 — Bitget, the world’s largest Universal Exchange (UEX), has launched H100USDT and B200USDT Pre-Market Compute Perpetuals, giving users access to perpetual contracts tracking NVIDIA H100 and B200 GPU rental prices. The launch marks a retail industry first for perpetual contracts linked to GPU rental-price indices. The contracts track the hourly rental cost of NVIDIA H100 and B200 GPU compute, turning one of the fundamental costs powering artificial intelligence into a tradable market.

GPUs have become critical infrastructure for training and running AI models. As investment in AI data centers accelerates, the cost of accessing high-performance compute is emerging as an economic signal in its own right, shaped by chip availability, cloud capacity and demand from AI companies. Traditional derivatives markets are beginning to develop around compute pricing, with CME Group scheduled to launch H100 and B200 GPU rental-price futures in October. 

Bitget is bringing this emerging market to retail traders through crypto-native derivatives. H100USDT and B200USDT Pre-Market Compute Perps track the H100 and B200 GPU Rental Price Indices published by Silicon Data, reflecting standardized average hourly rental costs across multiple GPU cloud and compute providers. Quoted against indices expressed in USD per GPU-hour and settled in USDT, the contracts trade 24/7 with leverage of up to 10x.

The indices standardize factors including GPU specifications, rental duration, geography and rental terms, creating a reference point for a market where pricing has historically been fragmented across cloud providers and private agreements. Traders can take a view on changes in compute prices and participate in their price discovery without purchasing GPUs or entering cloud rental agreements.
